notes: Isolates finding three seeded defects in a small module against a written spec: an initialisation bug (best = 0 breaks all-negative input), an off-by-one window range, and the same off-by-one repeated in a second function, with a third function that is already correct as a control against blind rewriting. Confound removed: no dependencies, no I/O, module-level behaviour is pure; the spec is restated in the prompt so the contract is not in doubt. Tier 2: two distinct defect classes plus one fix that must be applied in two places; strong-model prior 70-90%. Grading scope: $OUT_DIR/window.py only, exercised over 22 fixed vectors (source: tests/vectors.json) in a subprocess with a scrubbed env and a 30s timeout; import-time output is a failure. False-positive audit: (a) the original buggy module, (b) only the range fixed (all-negative still fails), (c) only best=None fixed (last window still missed), (d) a module that prints on import, (e) no file - all rejected.
contamination_source: original (sliding-window off-by-one and max-initialisation are classic defect classes; the module, spec and vectors are bespoke)
